guest_lever_verbatim.title: E-Q7: knife-edge-checkerboard-cascade under S3 row-major LWW, seeded at the uncoupled exact-zero boundary sigma=2/3
guest_lever_verbatim.why: C4 is the last open claim a single registered run can decisively falsify, and wave-34 handed us both the pinned write order (S3 LIVE-READ ROW-MAJOR LWW, EQ6-D1 PASS) and the exact adversarial point (2/3, acc=-2; float class 0, fixed class +1; 5acc+8r=0 family) where the two planes disagree by one S-unit. Registering situation 9 on that point tests C4 and re-tests the R8 fixed plane in one run.
guest_lever_verbatim.cheapest_decisive_run: Reuse qthe_fixed.mjs (DEFAULT_SIGMA_Q=6807362106) and the EQ6-D1 fresh-rerun harness. Substrate: 64x1 all-Abstain d=0, T=64, 4096 write attempts, real kernel write path, no mocks. Three arms: sigma=2/3 (coupled boundary), sigma=8/5, sigma=7/10. Point prediction (frozen before run): C4 is CONFIRMED iff the checkerboard parity flips at least once per tick under row-major LWW and terminal occupancy is parity-dependent; C4 is FALSIFIED iff terminal occupancy is parity-independent (cascade collapses to uniform) in all three arms. Falsifier: any arm where the float and fixed planes diverge by more than the pre-registered one S-unit, or where EQ6-D1 byte-identity fails across fresh reruns. Cost: one cooker run, three arms, ~12k write attempts, no new code beyond a sigma parameter sweep; receipt = commit SHA + chain tip + per-arm byte-identical rerun log.
residual_risks_sealed_by_guest: C4 may be under-specified: 'cascade' could mean per-tick propagation depth or terminal occupancy; if the floor is not frozen to one of these before the run, a PASS/FAIL will be re-litigable.

The one-S-unit boundary disagreement is absorbing (fixed term 8589934593 = 2S+1), so a cascade seeded exactly there may be trivially frozen rather than knife-edge — the run must include a neighboring sigma (e.g. 8/5 and 7/10) to show the cascade is not an artifact of the absorbing point.
C1 remains open and unaddressed by this lever; if C4 passes, C1 becomes the next bottleneck and will need its own situation.

source_situation_verbatim.name: knife-edge-checkerboard-cascade
source_situation_verbatim.description: A 128x64 substrate is tiled in a strict checkerboard of Attract (tau=1) and Repel (tau=2) cells, with a thin Ground (tau=0) seam down the central column and a handful of Abstain (tau=3) cells planted on the seam. At tick 0 exactly one border cell on the seam has its byte flipped from Attract to Repel. The substrate must decide, within a bounded tick window, whether the flip is absorbed locally or propagates across the whole board via Moore-8 real-accumulator pressure (M5) and wormhole bridges (M4). Theta (C4) is swept across the knife edge where the two outcomes trade dominance.
source_situation_verbatim.substrate_spec: w=128, h=64, seed=1337. tau = 1 if (x+y) mod 2 == 0 else 2, for all cells with x != 63; central column x=63 forced to tau=0 (Ground seam); at (63, y) for y in {8, 24, 40, 56} place tau=3 (Abstain) with d = 32; all d initialised to 32 except the flipped cell at (64, 32) which is set to tau=2, d=32 at tick 0.
source_situation_verbatim.task: Detect whether the single flipped byte produces a substrate-wide phase inversion (>=90% of originally-Attract cells flipping sign of their real accumulator by tick T=256) or dies within a radius r<=4 of the flip site.
source_situation_verbatim.metric: For each (wormhole_state, theta) arm: ticks-to-global-inversion, final inversion fraction, and the radius of the dead-flip case at tick 256. Trace hash sealed per arm (M6).
source_situation_verbatim.floor: Pre-registered: wormhole ON at theta=pi/4 must reach >=90% inversion in <=128 ticks in at least 4 of 5 seeds; wormhole OFF must fail to reach >=50% inversion in >=4 of 5 seeds. If both arms land in the same regime at theta=pi/4, C4's claimed threshold is falsified for this substrate.
